title: Sell Mineral Rights in Export, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Export, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Export, Westmoreland County? We buy Marcellus royalty and mineral interests in this old coal-shipping borough. Fair look, no pressure.
heroLead: Export got its name from the coal that used to leave town by rail, and a lot of the same acreage that fed those old mines is now sitting under Marcellus units.
intro: Export is a small Westmoreland County borough that grew up around coal shipping, and like a lot of towns in this corner of the county, the mineral history under the ground didn't stop at coal. Families who held onto farmland near Level Green and the Trafford line often ended up with oil and gas rights that got leased decades after the coal was already gone.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around Export and the surrounding townships. If your interest is producing under an active unit, tied up in an old lease nobody's looked at in years, or split among several heirs, we'd like to hear the details.

sections.heading: Westmoreland's place in the Marcellus SW play
paragraphs: Westmoreland County sits within reach of the Marcellus wet-gas fairway, with EQT and CNX both active on leases across the county, though development here has been less concentrated than in Washington or Greene. Around Export specifically, tracts tend to be smaller and more residential than the big farm units further south, which changes how pooling and unit size typically work.
Older gas history matters too — this part of Westmoreland had shallow gas wells long before Marcellus, and some families still hold interests tied to those legacy leases alongside anything newer.

sections.heading: What coal-era deeds mean for your title
paragraphs: Because Export was a coal town, plenty of local deeds from the early 1900s severed coal rights from oil, gas, and surface separately. That's normal here, but it means a title search on Export-area land often turns up more than one prior severance, and we make sure we understand which one actually covers oil and gas before we make an offer.

sections.heading: Getting a real number for your interest
paragraphs: Value depends on whether your interest is producing, leased-but-idle, or open, plus lease terms and nearby well activity — we don't quote anything until we've actually reviewed your documents.
Send whatever you have, even a partial lease or an old royalty stub, and we'll walk you through what we can offer and why.

faqs.question: Is Export, PA in the core Marcellus wet-gas area?
faqs.answer: It's within reach of the Westmoreland County Marcellus play, but activity here tends to be lighter and more scattered than in core counties like Washington or Greene, so tract-by-tract activity matters more than a general county label.

faqs.question: My Export-area land has an old coal deed. Does that stop me from selling oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: Not usually. Coal was frequently severed separately from oil and gas in this part of Westmoreland County, so we just need to confirm which document actually controls the oil and gas interest before moving forward.

faqs.question: What if my lease is decades old and I don't know if it's still active?
faqs.answer: Send us what you have. We regularly review older leases to determine whether they're still held by production or otherwise in effect before discussing a purchase.
